name: Maryland
agency: Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Natural Resources Police

rule.hpNote: any vessel for pleasure that must be numbered (registered), no hp threshold
rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after July 1, 1972 needs a certificate of boating safety education to run a registered (numbered) recreational boat in Maryland, including a PWC.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de julio de 1972 o después necesita el certificado de educación en seguridad náutica para manejar una embarcación recreativa registrada en Maryland, incluidas las motos acuáticas.

minAge.note: Under 16: must hold a certificate and be supervised aboard by a certified person (18+ if the boat is 11 ft or longer), or by someone born before July 1, 1972.

exemptions: Out-of-state residents visiting 60 days or less in a boat numbered elsewhere, if 16+ or holding a NASBLA certificate.
Foreign visitors for 90 days or less in a foreign boat.
A U.S. Coast Guard license, or a USCG Auxiliary, Power Squadron or school certificate, counts as the certificate.

card.feeNote: The state replaces lost certificates it issued free of charge; a 30-day temporary certificate (renewable once) can be issued on affidavit.

nonResident: NASBLA-approved certificates from other states are accepted; visitors 16+ in a boat numbered in another state are exempt for up to 60 days.
rental: Liveries renting boats under 16 ft must themselves hold a boating safety certificate; no renter exemption is stated in the statute.
penalty: Misdemeanor: up to $25 first offense, up to $500 for a repeat within 2 years; enforced only as a secondary action.
